resources.string: How the deltoid raises the arm
Deltoid and arm elevation
A simplified side view of normal arm elevation. Depth is opened up to show all three parts. The poses are illustrative, not measured angles or a fixed sequence of muscle activation.
Three parts, one attachment
The front part starts at the outer clavicle, the middle part at the acromion, and the rear part at the scapular spine. All three converge at the deltoid tuberosity on the humerus.
The upper arm lifts

As the arm moves out to the side, the middle deltoid helps turn the humerus upward. The rotator cuff helps keep the humeral head centered; the relative contribution of each deltoid part varies with the direction of the lift.
The blade turns with the arm

The humerus rises at the shoulder joint while the scapula also rotates upward, turning the socket up. The clavicle moves with the shoulder girdle. These movements overlap and vary with the path of the arm.
The arm lowers smoothly
As the arm returns, the upper arm and shoulder blade move back together. In a controlled descent, the arm elevators can stay active as they lengthen, helping to slow the pull of gravity.
